text:
Thomas Harley plays 25 minutes a night for Dallas and still ends up in trade columns, the latest asking whether Toronto would pay a big price for him (NHL Trade Talk). That's speculation, not reporting, but it tells you how the league sees him: a big left-shot defenseman who carries the puck and plays in every situation. He had four points in six games at the Olympics for Canada.

His season so far is a tale of one goal. He has eight points in 16 games, and only one goal, which came on Nov. 1, on 31 shots. That's a shooting rate around 3%, half his usual, on chances that are slightly better than last season's. The Stars are getting 54.5% of the 5v5 chances with him on, six points better than without him, and he's playing more over his last ten games. We'd expect the goals to come. The question mark is defense: Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more with him on the ice in 2025-26 (bottom 10% of defensemen), and rated him around replacement level overall. Our projection is about 45 points, ahead of last season's 36.
headline: Thomas Harley is owed a few goals
